card.hook: Piles of fruit, fish, shell necklaces and stacks of hats are all crammed within arm's reach, so your camera roll is going to fill up fast. Start with one big wide picture before you dive in.
card.stand_here: Stand on Rue François Cardella, about 10 m south-east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face north-west. From here you can take a first wide shot before going closer.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the general view of the market and its stalls. Go to 0.5x for a roomier shot of the entrance or a busy aisle, then try 2x or more (depending on your phone) for close-ups of shell necklaces or fruit.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and put a row of stalls or a doorway along one of the lines for a tidy, balanced picture.
card.best_time: Morning is likely to be the liveliest time, with the most stalls busy. Check locally before you go for current times.
card.selfie_here: Stand in front of the main entrance, where the market's name is displayed, and use the front camera at 0.5x so the sign fits over your shoulder. The harbour boulevard (Boulevard Pomare) just outside the market doors is another spot to try with the market behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: If a stallholder is the main subject of your picture, ask first and be ready to buy a small souvenir or just say thank you. Tap water in Tahiti isn't always drinkable, so bring bottled water.
card.challenge: Find the most colourful pile of fruit you can and fill the whole frame with it, with the other stalls blurry behind.
card.good_to_know: Papeete Market is also known locally as Marché Papeete or the municipal market. It's a large market place in Papeete, the capital of Tahiti. You'll find fruit, vegetables, fish, oils, local textiles and handicrafts like hats, handbags and shell necklaces. It's a public market, so check locally before you go for current opening arrangements.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Rue François Cardella, about 10 m south-east of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face north-west. From here you can take a first wide shot before going closer.

The two selfie spots are inferred from page descriptions of the market's entrance and its frontage. They are not explicit selfie recommendations, so verify on site. Market opening hours vary between sources, so check before going.

card.hook: Picture white walls, a blue tile roof and a little gold angel on top of a slim spire, all set against Tahiti's green palms and bright sky. It's a colourful stop, and it's easy to photograph.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, in the front gardens on the main-road side. Face the temple's front, so the flags and gardens are in front of you and the spire rises behind them.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the whole front with the gardens and flags. If you're close and the spire won't fit, drop to zoom 0.5x. Then try zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the spire and the gold statue.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the spire on one of the vertical lines, then tap the white wall and slide it a little darker so the walls keep their detail and the sky stays blue.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning or late in the afternoon, when the light is softer and the grounds are quieter. Strong midday sun can make those white walls look harsh.
card.selfie_here: Try the landscaped gardens around the temple, with the flowers and palms behind you. Use the front camera, hold it a bit lower and tilt it up so the spire stays in the wider frame over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the front grounds facing the temple entrance, with the gardens, flags and spire in view, while you pose in the gardens in front of the building.
card.rules_and_safety: Please keep to the paths. Photos aren't allowed inside the temple, and only church members with a current temple recommend can go in, so enjoy the grounds from outside. Keep your voice down and dress modestly.
card.challenge: Get the gold angel, a flag and the blue roof all in one shot without the building leaning back. Step back and zoom in rather than tilting the phone up.
card.good_to_know: The temple was first dedicated in October 1983, closed in 2005 for a big renovation, and rededicated in November 2006. The spire is about 66 feet (around 20 metres) tall, and the walls are stucco mixed with imported white sand. In 2009 the church added gardens, parking and a straightened access road, so you can now see the building from the street much more easily.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, in the front gardens on the main-road side. Face the temple's front, so the flags and gardens are in front of you and the spire rises behind them.

selfie_spots.name: Gardens on the temple grounds, Route de Fautaua-Titioro
selfie_spots.detail: in the landscaped gardens around the temple, with the grounds' flowers and palms behind you
selfie_spots.why: Guides describe the grounds as flower-filled and palm-lined, giving a scenic backdrop for photos while the spire stays in the wider frame.

The temple itself is reserved for members in good standing, but the grounds are open to the public, so stay on the grounds and do not enter the building. No page states rules on selfie sticks or tripods. Sources disagree on the commune: most say Papeete, but Photogent says the temple is in Pirae. The Evendo page also advises modest dress and a quiet manner, which is conduct guidance, not a photo rule.

card.hook: Turn your back on the harbour and you'll find a park that comes with its own picture frame: a row of trees along the avenue, with green lawns tucked behind them.
card.stand_here: Stand on Avenue du Général de Gaulle, on the waterfront side directly opposite Parc Bougainville, with the harbour behind you. The park is to the north-west, about 1 minute on foot, so face north-west and shoot across to the park's edge.
card.zoom: Start at 1x so the trees can make a loose border around the park's edge. If the pavement is narrow and you can't step back, switch to 0.5x. Save 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for the bronze bust and the cannons.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the park's edge on the lower third, so the road stays small and the green is what people notice.
card.best_time: Late afternoon towards sunset is lovely, because the sky can add colour behind the lawns and trees. Earlier in the day is better for a plain, clear shot of the bust.
card.selfie_here: Stand along the waterfront side of the park with your back to the harbour view. Use the front camera, and try 0.5x if your phone has it, to fit in the boats and mountains over your shoulder. For a leafier selfie, the footbridge inside the park is a raised spot with the park's greenery behind you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to face the bronze bust and memorial at the park entrance, so both cannons fit in the frame, while you stand in front of the bust.
card.rules_and_safety: Take care when standing near the avenue and watch for traffic. Check the official site before you go for any access restrictions.
card.challenge: Take one picture where the tree trunks frame the park, with no bins or bare patches sneaking in. Spotting them is half the fun.
card.good_to_know: Parc Bougainville is a green public park in the middle of Papeete, directly across the avenue from the waterfront. A bronze bust of the navigator stands at the entrance, with the park's trees and cannons around it. Some areas are a bit worn, so it can look less tidy in person than in glossy photos.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Avenue du Général de Gaulle, on the waterfront side directly opposite Parc Bougainville, with the harbour behind you. The park is to the north-west, about 1 minute on foot, so face north-west and shoot across to the park's edge.

card.hook: Picture a ferry gliding past Moorea while a row of palms points right at it. That's the Paofai Gardens shot, and you get it just by strolling.
card.stand_here: Stand on the waterfront promenade, Avenue Pouvana'a a Oopa, along the lagoon edge of the gardens. Face out toward Moorea and turn away from the port.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the promenade and the palms. Tap 0.5x to fit the whole walkway and the sky in, then try 2x or more (if your phone has it) to pull Moorea and the ferries closer.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines, put the line of palms on one third of the frame and the lagoon and Moorea on the other, then tap Moorea so it's nice and sharp.
card.best_time: Go in late afternoon, when the light turns soft and warm. It's the best time for the sea view.
card.selfie_here: Head into the gardens to the koi ponds, away from the main promenade, and use your front camera with the colourful fish and plants around you. It works best as a close-up, since we can't promise the whole garden fits in behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The gardens are a public seafront park, but check the official site before you go for opening times and any closed areas. Playgrounds have reportedly been closed at times, so don't plan a picture around them.
card.challenge: Catch a ferry sliding past Moorea with the palms leading your eye in, and try a Live Photo so the boat actually moves.
card.good_to_know: Paofai Gardens is a green park on Papeete's waterfront, with palms, lawns, ponds and a paved walkway along the lagoon edge. Inside, the ponds hold koi and aquatic plants, and statues and memorials stand against the lawns. The harbour side can show shipping docks and a cargo yard, so keep your phone pointed toward Moorea.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the waterfront promenade, Avenue Pouvana'a a Oopa, along the lagoon edge of the gardens. Face out toward Moorea and turn away from the port.

selfie_spots.why: The colourful fish and aquatic plants give close-up shots with the garden greenery around you, though the sources do not describe the gardens as the backdrop for a full-frame selfie.

card.hook: A bright yellow town hall tucked behind tropical trees is about as easy as phone photography gets. Give it a few minutes and a handful of frames, then move on.
card.stand_here: Stand on Rue des Remparts, on the pavement facing the town hall, so the building sits behind its garden.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the whole front with the trees in front of it. If you're too close for it to fit, switch to 0.5x and keep the phone level. Then try zoom 2x (higher zooms depend on your phone) for a doorway or a window.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and line up the building's upright edges with them, then tap the yellow wall and slide it a little darker if the sky looks washed out.
card.best_time: Soft morning light suits the yellow front best. The gardens look their best in the hour before sunset, so that's a lovely time for people pictures.
card.selfie_here: Head into the gardens in front of the main facade and stand on the lawns or paths with the yellow front behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x if your phone offers it, and keep the building over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on Rue des Remparts facing the town hall, while you stand in the garden in front of the building, so the facade and clock tower fit in one frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Photographing the exterior and public areas is generally fine, but don't photograph people without asking. If you go inside, ask before taking any photos or videos, as some areas may be restricted.
card.challenge: Take your wide shot first, then hunt for one small detail, like a doorway, a window or tree shadows on the yellow wall, and see if it beats the big picture.
card.good_to_know: This is the Mairie de Papeete, the town hall, a yellow building with a colonial-style front in grounds full of tropical trees. The address is given as either Rue des Remparts or Avenue du Général de Gaulle, so check on the day. Be considerate of other people around you.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Rue des Remparts, on the pavement facing the town hall, so the building sits behind its garden. Follow the phone icon on the map: the town hall is to the south-west of it, about 1 minute on foot.

selfie_spots.why: Several guides describe the yellow colonial-style facade and its surrounding gardens as photogenic, with the gardens looking best in the hour before sunset.

card.hook: A bright yellow church with a red spire sounds like it might clash with the tropics. It doesn't. Against green leaves and a tropical sky, it looks great on a phone screen.
card.stand_here: Stand in Parc Bougainville, and the cathedral is to the east, about 5 minutes on foot. Face east and let the trees make a frame around the building. It's a calmer spot than the square out front.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole building and the trees around it. Then try 1x for a more natural look. Use zoom 2x or more (higher zooms depend on your phone) to pick out the red spire and bell tower.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and hold your phone level so the walls and bell tower stay upright. Let branches and leaves form the edges and put the cathedral in the middle.
card.best_time: Go in the golden hour before sunset. If the sky looks washed out, tap the yellow wall and drag the brightness down a little so the red spire keeps its colour.
card.selfie_here: Head to Place Notre Dame, the square in front of the cathedral. Stand facing the yellow front with the facade behind you, use the front camera, and try zoom 0.5x to fit the building over your shoulder. Early or late light also means fewer crowds.
card.ask_someone: In Parc Bougainville, ask a passer-by for a wide shot of you with the greenery around you and the cathedral behind.
card.rules_and_safety: It's a working church, so if you step inside, keep your phone quiet and respectful. Check the official site before you go for visiting times and dress expectations.
card.challenge: Play 'find the spire'. Take a few steps in different directions and see where the red spire pops out against the sky and where it vanishes.
card.good_to_know: Papeete Cathedral opened in 1875 and is the oldest Catholic church on the island. It's named after Notre Dame de Paris. Inside, look for the full-size Madonna and Child carving from the Marquesas Islands, where the child holds a breadfruit.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Parc Bougainville, and the cathedral is to the east, about 5 minutes on foot. Face east and let the trees make a frame around the building. It's a calmer spot than the square out front.

card.hook: Forget a grand monument. This is a modest, practical house on a hillside, with a verandah, tall palms and frangipani crowding in around it. The garden is the star, and the house just happens to live in it.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, in the garden at Maison James Norman Hall, and face the house. If a plant blocks your view, shuffle a few steps sideways rather than zooming in.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to show the whole house with its plants around it. If the grounds are tight and you can't step back, try 0.5x. Then use 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for the verandah, shutters and flowers.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the house on one third of the frame and let the palms and flowering shrubs fill the rest, and tap the house, then slide it darker if the bright sky turns the walls pale.
card.best_time: Go in the morning or late afternoon, when the light is softer and the garden colours look richer. Midday sun makes harsh patches of light and shade under the trees.
card.selfie_here: Take it in the garden at the front of the house, with the green façade behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x if you want more house in the shot, and keep the façade over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand in the garden facing the green façade so the whole house fits in the frame, while you pose in the garden in front of it.
card.rules_and_safety: Check the official site before you go to confirm whether the house and grounds are open and whether photography is allowed inside. Skip the hill above the house, as visiting the grave there needs permission.
card.challenge: Find a clear gap between the plants and get the house, a palm and a flower all in one shot. Bonus points if the verandah roof line stays dead straight.
card.good_to_know: James Norman Hall settled in Tahiti in 1924 and built this house himself in 1926. He co-wrote the three volumes of The Bounty Trilogy here between 1932 and 1934. Inside you'll find his 3,000-volume library and his typewriter, and the house opened as a museum on 17 January 2002.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, in the garden at Maison James Norman Hall, and face the house. If a plant blocks your view, shuffle a few steps sideways rather than zooming in.

selfie_research.notes: No page found gives a selfie-specific spot or a photo-taking tip, so both selfie spots are inferred from general descriptions of the garden and the tea room terrace; the second is weak. No page states rules about selfie sticks or tripods. The Visual Itineraries page says one of Hall's grandsons still lives on the property and visitors need permission to visit the grave on the hill above the house, so do not suggest going there. Per US News, the museum is open Tuesday to Saturday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., so check hours before visiting. The landmark is at Arue, not central Papeete, and the address is PK 5 côté montagne, Arue.
